_strings.@@10fdca9b45b6: Idaho Grocery Credit (Food Tax Credit) — Idaho residents only. Claimed for yourself, spouse, and each qualifying Idaho-resident dependent. If someone else can claim you as a dependent, you cannot claim it. Does NOT qualify for any month (or part of a month) a person received federal food stamp (SNAP) assistance, was incarcerated, or lived illegally in the US. Members of the Armed Forces domiciled in Idaho can take it; nonresidents under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act cannot. Refundable even if you are not required to file an income tax return (file Form 40, or Form 24 if not filing — Form 24 due by April 15, 2025).

_strings.@@db04e4592bdd: Treaty conformity — ID conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from ID income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the ID return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Idaho's resident return (Form 40) starts on line 7 from federal adjusted gross income (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 11), and the only statutory additions are on Form 39R, Part A (2024 instructions pp.30-31): federal NOL deduction, capital loss carryover incurred outside the state before becoming an Idaho resident, non-Idaho state/local bond interest and dividends, Idaho college savings account withdrawal, bonus depreciation, and other additions. There is NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (unlike CA's Schedule CA). Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and is not added back, it flows through untaxed. Idaho also affirmatively confirms this in its Noncitizens guidance (re-fetched live this session): 'Idaho honors all tax treaties recognized by the United States' and 'Gross income amounts exempt by treaty are not included in the gross income filing requirement for Idaho.' Therefore Idaho conforms to federal treaty exemptions.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 40, line 20: 'Tax from worksheet. See instructions, page 9.' Worksheet (2024 instructions p.9): 1. 'Enter the amount of Idaho taxable income from Form 40, line 19'; 2. 'Enter the amount shown below for your filing status: Single or married filing separately, enter $4,673 — Married filing jointly, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse, enter $9,346'; 3. 'Subtract line 2 from line 1. Enter the subtotal'; 4. 'Multiply subtotal by 5.695%'; 5. 'Idaho tax. Enter the total here and on Form 40, line 20. If zero or less, enter zero.' Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,550 — NOT an exemption and NOT applied by calc.state_tax — it is an ADDITIONAL STANDARD DEDUCTION: $1,550 per age-65-or-older box checked on Form 40 line 12a ($1,950 instead if single or head of household), added to the base standard deduction via the Standard Deduction Worksheet, line 5 (2024 instructions pp.8-9; born before January 2, 1960). Boxes must match the federal return.); blind ($1,550 — NOT an exemption and NOT applied by calc.state_tax — it is an ADDITIONAL STANDARD DEDUCTION: $1,550 per blind box checked on Form 40 line 12b ($1,950 instead if single or head of household), added to the base standard deduction via the Standard Deduction Worksheet, line 5 (2024 instructions pp.8-9). Boxes must match the federal return.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 CHANGE — RATE CUT AND RE-INDEXED FLOOR: 'Effective January 1, 2024, the individual income tax rate is 5.695%' (What's New, p.1) — down from 2023's 5.8% — and the Line 20 worksheet's zero-floor subtraction amounts were re-indexed to $4,673 (single/MFS) and $9,346 (MFJ/HOH/QSS), from 2023's $4,489/$8,978. Do not use the 2023 rate or amounts for 2024. Base guidance: Supply Form 40, line 11 'Total Adjusted Income' = federal AGI (Form 40 line 7, from federal Form 1040/1040-SR line 11) plus Form 39R Part A additions minus Form 39R Part B subtractions. With no Idaho additions or subtractions this equals federal AGI. The op subtracts only the per-status standard deduction (Form 40 line 16); if you claim the federal qualified business income deduction (Form 40 line 18 = federal 1040 line 13) or itemize (Form 40 lines 13-15), the op will overstate tax — subtract your line 18 QBI amount from line 11 before supplying it, or compute on the form. Structure: Idaho's 2024 tax is a single 5.695% rate on Idaho taxable income ABOVE a filing-status threshold — $4,673 (single or married filing separately) / $9,346 (married filing jointly, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse) — per the Form 40 line 20 worksheet (2024 instructions p.9). It is modeled here as a 0% bracket up to the threshold and 5.695% above it; taxable income at or below the threshold owes $0. Head of household uses the SAME $9,346 worksheet threshold as married filing jointly (instructions p.9), even though its standard deduction ($21,900) differs from MFJ's ($29,200). Qualifying surviving spouse (Form 40 filing status 5) is listed in the worksheet with the same $9,346 amount as married filing jointly, so the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping is exact for both the brackets and the $29,200 standard deduction. The 2024 worksheet prints an explicit zero clause — line 5: 'If zero or less, enter zero' (new wording versus 2023, which left it implicit); the 0% floor bracket implements the $0 result for taxable income at or below the subtraction amount. Qualified business income deduction NOT modeled: Form 40 line 18 subtracts the federal QBI deduction (federal 1040/1040-SR line 13) AFTER the standard/itemized deduction to reach Idaho taxable income (line 19). See base guidance for how to account for it. Itemizers NOT modeled: Form 40 lines 13-15 use federal Schedule A itemized deductions MINUS state and local income or general sales taxes (line 14 addback), and Idaho lets you ADD any federal foreign tax credit amount to Idaho itemized deductions ('If you claim the federal foreign tax credit, Idaho allows that amount as a deduction'); filers use the LARGER of net itemized or the standard deduction. The op applies only the standard deduction. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled (Standard Deduction Worksheet and 'You Must Itemize If', 2024 instructions p.8): married filing separately MUST itemize if the spouse itemizes; dual-status nonresident aliens must itemize; a person claimable as another's dependent is limited to the greater of $1,300 or earned income + $450 (capped at the status amount); age-65+/blind boxes add $1,550 per box ($1,950 if single or head of household). Compute those cases on the worksheet. Idaho has NO personal or dependent exemptions ('Idaho conforms to the Internal Revenue Code (IRC), which no longer allows personal exemptions' — Noncitizens guidance). The per-person amounts on the return are TAX CREDITS subtracted from tax, not base reductions, and are not modeled: the Idaho Child Tax Credit is $205 per qualifying child age 16 or under (Form 40 line 25, nonrefundable), and the grocery credit is $120 per qualifying person ($140 if 65+) (Form 40 line 43, refundable). $10 Permanent Building Fund (PBF) tax (Form 40 line 32) is a separate flat tax owed by everyone required to file an Idaho return (waived for those below the filing threshold ('NRF'), recipients of Idaho public assistance at year-end, and the legally blind). It is outside the line 20 computation and NOT modeled. No tax-table mandate: the 2024 booklet contains no tax tables — every filer computes line 20 with the worksheet, so bracket math reproduces the form exactly (whole-dollar rounding aside). Part-year residents and nonresidents file Form 43, not Form 40; Form 43 line 42 uses the identical worksheet (same $4,673/$9,346 amounts, same 5.695%) applied to Form 43 line 41 Idaho taxable income (2024 instructions p.34). See instructions, page 9', line 19 reads 'Idaho taxable income. Subtract line 18 from line 17. If less than zero, enter zero', and the line-16 margin prints the standard deduction amounts ($14,600 single/MFS, $21,900 HOH, $29,200 MFJ).
